prompt: Part of me is furious at my coworker for taking credit, while another part feels ashamed for caring so much about status.
I keep fighting the anxiety before every presentation, and the more I try to push it down, the louder it gets.
Everything in my life feels like an emergency right now and I want to blow up the whole project just to feel relief.
My chest has been tight all week after that argument with my brother, even though my head says it's over.
A protective part of me wants to cut everyone off so I don't disappoint them, yet I feel lonely without my community.
I know what matters to me, but grief over what I lost keeps me frozen at the threshold.
I can't control whether the layoffs hit my team tomorrow, and my thoughts keep spiraling into worst-case scenarios.
My shoulders are up around my ears from trying to force a decision that isn't ready yet.
The inner critic won't stop narrating every mistake I made today, and I'm exhausted from arguing with it.
We talked last week about my perfectionism at work. Today I shipped something imperfect and didn't collapse, though I still feel restless.
Following up on my caregiver burnout: I finally asked my sister for help this weekend, and the guilt hit harder than expected.
The anniversary we noted last month is tomorrow. My body feels heavy, and I don't want to rush past it.
